files.Web/index.html:
{{NAME}}

Made with Lamp.

declared.package: rm -f build/app.zip && mkdir -p build && cd Web && zip -qr ../build/app.zip .
declared.rules: The app is a web page in Web/ (HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no build step and no frameworks from the network), shown full screen at 1920x1080 on the Xbox in Lamp's host for Microsoft Edge's Chromium web view (WebView2), served from the package at https://lamp.example/: modern JavaScript and CSS work, as in a current Chrome, and so does WebGL 2. The page is 1920x1080 CSS pixels, as in the preview. Design for a TV across the room: large type (36px and up), high contrast, nothing that scrolls the whole page. It's driven by the controller: Lamp's lamp.js gives the d-pad and left stick as the arrow keys, A as Enter (which also presses the focused element) and B as Escape, and the other buttons as keys named GamepadX, GamepadY, GamepadLeftShoulder, GamepadRightShoulder, GamepadLeftTrigger, GamepadRightTrigger, GamepadMenu and GamepadView; read e.key, never e.keyCode. Give every control the class `focusable` and a visible :focus style, and use the arrow-focus code in app.js; B (Escape) goes back a screen, and on the first screen does nothing, since the app stays open. index.html loads Lamp's lamp.js before app.js; keep it so. Lamp wraps Web/ into a signed Windows package itself. console.log, console.error and uncaught errors go to the app's log on the Xbox, which look_at_app with on_device shows beside the console's own screenshot: look there to see how it really runs. A 3D game or scene uses three.js, which Lamp puts in Web/three: in index.html put the import map <script type="importmap">{ "imports": { "three": "./three/three.module.js", "three/addons/": "./three/addons/" } }</script> before a <script type="module"> for the game, then import * as THREE from 'three' and addons from 'three/addons/…' (OrbitControls, GLTFLoader and the like; nothing else is there, so no Draco or KTX2 files). Draw with new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true }), setPixelRatio(devicePixelRatio) and setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight) on a full-screen canvas so it draws at 1920x1080, and resize it on window resize. An Xbox One is a modest console: draw many copies of one shape as one THREE.InstancedMesh, never as hundreds of separate meshes, reuse geometries and materials, keep to MeshStandardMaterial or cheaper, one or two lights and no real-time shadows, and aim for 60 frames a second. In a game, read the controller directly each frame while it's played with navigator.getGamepads()[0] (the standard mapping: axes 0 and 1 the left stick, 2 and 3 the right, with a dead zone of about 0.15; buttons[0] A, [1] B, [2] X, [3] Y, [4] and [5] the bumpers, [6] and [7] the triggers' value, [12] to [15] the d-pad), and ignore the arrow and Enter keys lamp.js sends meanwhile. Shake the controller with the standard gp.vibrationActuator.playEffect('dual-rumble', { duration, strongMagnitude, weakMagnitude }) ('trigger-rumble' with leftTrigger and rightTrigger for the triggers' own motors), which Lamp's host plays on the controller; keep each effect short (under a second) and call it again for a long rumble. Take the keyboard too, as the same moves (WASD or the arrows, Space, Enter, Escape for B): that's how the game is played in the preview on the person's Mac, where you try it with use_app, holding a key with amount in seconds.

app.purpose: an app or a game, 3D games included: what nearly every Xbox wish is

lines: Join the Microsoft developer program at the link (one-time fee)
On the Xbox, install Xbox Dev Mode from the Store
Open it and enter its code at aka.ms/activatexbox
Back on the Xbox, choose Switch and restart
In Dev Home, open Remote Access Settings
steps.title: Switch the Xbox to Developer Mode

lines: In Remote Access Settings, choose Set username and password
Use lamp as the user name, and pick a password
steps.title: Give Lamp the Device Portal password

game.purpose: only a heavy 3D game the wish says needs the console's full power (a big world, many things moving at once, fast action) or native code; it needs a 2 GB download first
